singles/stewart-cadets/.title: Stewart Cadets
singles/stewart-cadets/.text:
[Dad calls each verse line. The boys echo it back.]

Dad: Stewart boys, fall in!

This is how we’ll handle you,
I won’t live inside a zoo!
Time to get this whole house clean,
March and scrub like a Marine!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
Dust bunnies are getting bold!
Grab the broom and sweep the floor,
Get the crumbs behind the door!
Sweep beneath each kitchen chair,
Bet you’ll find some crackers there!
Get the corners by the wall,
Grab the dustpan, dump it all!

Socks and shirts go in the bin,
If you miss, then try again!
Fold your shirts and match each pair,
Put clean clothes away with care!

Scrape your plate and grab your cup,
Take them both when you get up!
Wash the front and wash the back,
Set them in the drying rack!

Dad: Sound off!
Boys: One, two!
Dad: Sound off!
Boys: Three, four!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
“Just a minute” gets real old!
When Mom calls, I pause my game,
First time that she says my name!

Ask before you take it out,
Wait for yes so there’s no doubt!
If they tell you no today,
Hands off, boys, and walk away!
If they lend their stuff to you,
Bring it back when you are through!

I don’t know but I’ve been told,
Truth is worth much more than gold!
Don’t give Dad an “I don’t know.”
If you did it, tell him so!

Skip your chores and here’s the drill,
Five push-ups, then scrub that spill!
If you man up, do it right,
No more drills for you tonight!

Dad: Who did it?
Boys: I did, sir!
Dad: Who cleans it?
Boys: I do, sir!
Dad: What’s better than gold?
Boys: Honesty is better than gold!

Dad: Sound off!
Boys: One, two!
Dad: Sound off!
Boys: Three, four!
All: One, two, three, four! One, two! Three, four!

singles/the-stewart-zoo/.title: THE STEWART ZOO
singles/the-stewart-zoo/.text:
[Intro]
[Animal noises: a puppy yip, a raptor screech, a bunny thump, a platypus growl, then drums kick in]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Welcome to the zoo!

[Verse 1]
Samuel has a platypus, the strangest pet in town,
A bill just like a duck and a beaver tail that flaps around.
He lays eggs, but he's a mammal, now isn't that absurd?
He's the weirdest, wonderfulest critter ever heard!

[Verse 2]
John has a puppy dog with ears that flop and flap,
He chews up every shoe and he curls up on your lap.
He wags his tail so hard that it knocks the lamp right down,
He's the goodest, bestest puppy in the whole wide town!

[Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets, and a house that's full of noise,
God made them all, and He made those boys!

[Verse 3]
Stephen has a raptor, feathers head to toe,
Turkey-sized and speedy, watch him go, go, go!
He tiptoes through the kitchen, “SKREE!” he wants a snack,
Mom says, “Not the pancakes!” and he gives them right back.

[Verse 4]
Daniel has a little bunny, Fu Fu is his name,
Twitchy nose and floppy ears, and he thumps when he's tame.
There's a rhyme about a Fu Fu who's a rascal, so they say,
But this Fu Fu's gentle, and he hops the nice way!

[Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets, and a house that's full of noise,
God made them all, and He made those boys!

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow and big]
“Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord!”
[Platypus growl]
[Puppy: yip yip!]
[Raptor: SKREE!]
[Bunny: thump thump!]
“A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast.”
That means be kind to every creature!
[Drums crash back in]
Even the raptor!

[Verse 5]
Now the puppy chases the raptor, and the raptor chases a sock,
Fu Fu thumps on the couch while the platypus watches the clock.
Mom walks in the room and says, “Who let the zoo inside?”
Four boys point at each other: “It was him! I just got here!”

[Final Chorus]
Four boys, four pets, what a crazy zoo!
Squeak and squawk and growl and yip, and a roar or two!
Four boys, four pets

singles/all-aboardwith-daniel/.title: All AboardWith Daniel
singles/all-aboardwith-daniel/.text:
[Intro]
[Train whistle, chugging drums, handclaps]
[Spoken, kid voice]
All aboard!

[Verse 1]
Chugga chugga, chugga chugga, down the track we go,
A little engine rolling through the valley, nice and slow.
Puffing up the hillside, steam up in the air,
Toot toot! He's got a job to do, and he's glad to be there!

[Chorus]
All aboard, all aboard,
Jesus is the engineer!
He knows every mile of the track,
And He'll bring us safely there!
Chugga chugga, toot toot,
Stay right on the line,
When you follow the One who made the road,
You're gonna be just fine!

[Verse 2]
The engine reached a bridge that looked too high to cross,
He puffed and said, "I'm just too small," and he nearly stopped.
But the engineer said, "Steady now, I'm right here with you,
I built this bridge, and I'll take you through!"

[Chorus]
All aboard, all aboard,
Jesus is the engineer!
He knows every mile of the track,
And He'll bring us safely there!
Chugga chugga, toot toot,
Stay right on the line,
When you follow the One who made the road,
You're gonna be just fine!

[Verse 3]
Two train cars were squabbling on the siding one day,
"I'm bigger!" "I'm faster!" "Get out of my way!"
But the little engine rolled in with a smile,
He said, "Let's pull together, it's a long, long mile!"

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow]
"Blessed are the peacemakers,
For

singles/no-more-stinky-elephants/.title: No More Stinky Elephants
singles/no-more-stinky-elephants/.text:
Verse 1
There was an elephant, big and round,
The stinkiest one in the whole playground!
He wiggled his ears, he wiggled his toes…
Everybody shouted, “Hold your nose!”

Chorus
🎶 No more stinky elephants!
No more stinky elephants!
Take a bath and scrub, scrub, scrub!
Bubble, bubble, rub, rub, rub!
No more stinky elephants!
Hooray! Hooray! Hooray! 🎶

Verse 2
He splashed in a tub with lots of foam,
Rubber ducks came floating home.
He washed his trunk from tip to tail…
Now he smells like lemon ale! (Or sing “lemon pie” if you prefer.)

Chorus
🎶 No more stinky elephants!
No more stinky elephants!
Take a bath and scrub, scrub, scrub!
Bubble, bubble, rub, rub, rub!
No more stinky elephants!
Hooray! Hooray! Hooray! 🎶

Ending
If your elephant starts to stink,
Don’t you worry—don’t you blink!
Grab some soap and sing along…
Then everybody ends with:

🎶 NO MORE STINKY ELEPHANTS! 🐘✨

singles/god-made-the-dinosaurs/.title: God Made the Dinosaurs
singles/god-made-the-dinosaurs/.text:
[Intro]
[Big stomping drums, a loud ROAR sound effect, handclaps]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Ready? Stomp with me!

[Verse 1]
Tyrannosaurus rex was the king of the land,
Big old teeth and a teeny little hand.
He couldn't clap, he couldn't tie a shoe,
But God made him special, and He made you too!

[Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Verse 2]
Triceratops had three horns on his face,
He stood up tall and held his place.
When a bully came around, he didn't run or hide,
He stood up for his friends with his dino pride!

[Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Verse 3]
Brachiosaurus had a neck so long,
He munched the treetop leaves all day long.
He looked way up, up, up so high,
And said, "Thank You, Lord, for the big blue sky!"

[Verse 4]
Stegosaurus had plates down his back,
A spiky tail and a stomp-stomp track.
He wasn't like the others, he was one of a kind,
And that's how God designed him, with His wonderful mind!

[Bridge]
[Drums drop out, handclaps only]
[Spoken, slow and big]
"And God made the beast of the earth after his kind,
And God saw that it was good!"
"I am fearfully and wonderfully made!"
[Drums crash back in]
That means you!

[Verse 5]
Now Stephen draws a T-Rex with a great big grin,
Dinosaurs everywhere, and he's just getting started!
He knows the God who made them is the God who made him,
And He loves every roar and every stomp!

[Final Chorus]
Stomp, stomp, stomp, stomp, ROAR!
God made the dinosaurs!
Big ones, small ones, spiky ones, tall ones,
God made the dinosaurs!
And God made YOU!
[Kids shout: ROAR!]

[Outro]
[Big stomp, then a tiny squeaky roar]
[Spoken, kid voice]
Okay, that last one was me.

[End]

singles/are-you-still-thankful/.title: Are You Still Thankful
singles/are-you-still-thankful/.text:
[Verse 1 — Soft, Searching]
There was a shoreline.
There was a grave.
There were the people
God helped sustain.

Then came the harvest,
Corn, fowl, and deer.
Neighbors sat with them.
Thanks mingled with tears.

[Pre-Chorus]
They knew the hunger.
They knew the cost.
Even in plenty,
They knew what they’d lost.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 2 — Slowly Building]
There was a nation,
Newly made free.
Washington called us
To bow gratefully.

Then came division,
Brothers at war.
Lincoln called wounded
Hearts to the Lord.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for His mercy,
Prayer for our land.
Even in sorrow,
We needed His hand.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 3 — Warm, Bittersweet]
Nineteen-fifty.
Chairs on the floor.
Grandma is coming;
One place for more.

Bread from the oven,
Hands worn with care.
Dad bows his head now.
We hear his prayer.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for the wages,
Thanks for the rain,
Thanks for the mercy
That brought us again.

[Verse 4 — Growing Urgency]
Now there is plenty,
More than we need.
Phones at the table,
No time to speak.

Christmas is calling.
Sales fill the screen.
We’re making our wishes.
What does thanks mean?

[Bridge — Exposed Voice]
Why did we gather?
What was this for?
When did our blessings
Leave us wanting more?

Lord, I’ve been asking.
Lord, I’ve forgot
How much You’ve given,
How much it cost.

[Final Chorus — Full, Aching]
Are we still thankful?
Lord, help us say yes.
More than a dinner,
More than a guest.

You give the harvest.
You give us breath.
Still we depend on
Your faithfulness.

[Outro — Quiet]
Before it is Christmas,
Let us stay here.
Thank You for mercy
Through all these years.

Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.

[Let the final piano chord fade]

singles/the-other-guy/.title: The Other Guy
singles/the-other-guy/.text:
[Spoken Intro: low male voice, solo piano]
You're the man you swore you'd never be,
And pride has hurt your family.

[Pause]
The drink's gone warm, you turn your ring,
And think of every broken thing.

Or on the couch, the TV black,
Her coat still hangs. You want her back.
A drawing on the fridge, you standing tall.
Your sons don't know the truth at all.

[Pause, spoken freely]
You remember the boy you were,
And the man you promised to become.

You didn't.

You can't see past the man you are.

[Piano drops to one low note]
But wait.

[Verse 1: minor key, sparse piano and cello]
There was a man who watched them die,
Sure that he served the Lord.
And another man stood tall at the top,
"I built it all," he roared.

[Low, almost spoken]
Pride buries the good.

[Verse 2]
There was a man who lied to live,
And his son would do the same.
And another man disowned his friend,
And could not bear the shame.

[Low, almost spoken]
Lies leave us alone.

[Verse 3]
There was a man who took a life,
And ran away to hide.
And another man took from his own,
And counted coins while they cried.

[Low, almost spoken]
Stains don't wash out.

[Verse 4]
There was a man no one could beat,
Who kept on falling the same old way.
And another man won the biggest fight,
Then ran, and begged to die that day.

[Low, almost spoken]
Despair says, "You're done."

[Chorus: stripped back, sorrowful]
We always thought He'd choose some other guy,
Someone strong enough to never ask Him why.
We're the men we swore we'd never be,
How could God use men like you and me?

[Spoken Bridge: piano only, almost a whisper]
"Man looketh on the outward appearance,
But the Lord looketh on the heart."

[Pause]

Then Someone called their names.

[Verse 5: key lifts, drums enter, strings begin to rise]
That man who watched the innocent die
Wrote of grace that set men free.
And that man at the top who said, "I built it all,"
Looked up, and learned to see.

Grace lifts the proud.

[Verse 6]
That man who lied to save his life
Learned to trust what God had vowed.
And that man who disowned his friend
Heard, "Feed My sheep," and bowed.

Truth makes honest men of liars.

[Verse 7]
That man who took a life
Came back, and led them through.
And that man who took from his own
Left his table, and wrote what's true.

Mercy washes what we can't.

[Verse 8]
That man no one could beat
Gave his last strength in one prayer.
And that man who hid and wished it over
Found God still waiting there.

Hope says, "You're not done."

[Chorus: full band, strong male vocal]
There was no other guy,
Thieves and liars, blood on their hands.
They were never the hero,
But the Hero made them heroes.

[Spoken Reveal: slow and deliberate, soft piano, one name per drum hit, pause between names]
Paul.
Babylon's king.
Abraham.
Peter.
Moses.
Matthew.
Samson.
Elijah.

[Drums stop]
Men who fell.
Men who ran.
And God still called their names.

[Pause, quiet]
"And such were some of you:
But ye are washed."

[Final Verse: quiet choir enters, gradually building]
And somewhere tonight a man's in the dirt,
With a secret he's carried for years.
The screen in the dark, the bottle he hides,
The anger, the shame, the tears.

The job he lost, the words he said,
The lie he's afraid to undo.
The voice that says, "You're done, you're through."

[Brief silence]
Get up. Someone's calling you.

[Final Chorus: full band and choir, triumphant key lift]
There is no other guy,
It was never the strength of the man.
We're not who we swore we'd be,
But He's the God who makes men new.

The true Hero shining through
Every broken life surrendered.
We've got nothing left to prove.
Here we are, Lord. Make us new.

[Spoken: band softens, sustained choir]
"My grace is sufficient for thee:
For my strength is made perfect in weakness."

[Outro: piano alone, very quiet]
"Wait on the Lord: be of good courage,
And he shall strengthen thine heart."

[Long pause]
But wait.

[End]

singles/before-we-hang-the-lights/.title: Before We Hang The Lights
singles/before-we-hang-the-lights/.text:
BEFORE WE HANG THE LIGHTS

[Intro: gentle piano and fingerpicked acoustic guitar]

[Verse 1: intimate male vocal]
There’s a box of lights beside the stairs,
The boys are pulling out their chairs.
Dawn brings the last dish through the door,
We make some room and pass one more.
Someone asks, “Can we hang these tonight?”
I look around in the soft white light.
“We will, but first, before we do,
Let’s name the things God brought us through.”

[Chorus: quiet, warm, prayerful]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
Let the dishes wait, let the room grow still,
There’s a place in us that only praise can fill.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
Let our children hear those stories clear,
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Verse 2]
I used to listen to my father pray,
And watch the steam drift slowly away.
I’d bow my head and peek to see
If he was nearly done so we could eat.
Now there are things I want these boys to know
That I was far too young to see back then.
I hear Dad thank the Lord for one more year,
And wish that I could hear that prayer again.

[Chorus: gentle harmonies]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
Let the dishes wait, let the room grow still,
There’s a place in us that only praise can fill.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
Let our children hear those stories clear,
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Bridge: piano softens, tender delivery]
We remember when the money was tight,
Counting what we had late into the night.
The times we thought we couldn’t carry on,
You gave us strength enough to face the dawn.

These are the altars of our lives,
The prayers we prayed, the help supplied.
We tell our boys what You have done,
So they know where our help comes from.

[Verse 3: tender, smiles through sadness]
We speak the names of those we miss,
Remember how they laughed and things they did.
An empty chair, a story told,
A little more their children get to hold.
We smile at something someone used to say,
Then wipe a quiet tear away.
Thank You for the years we got to share,
For love we carry past an empty chair.

[Final Chorus: fuller harmonies, still restrained]
Before we hang the lights this year,
Let’s thank the One who brought us here.
For those we miss and those we’re holding near,
For grace that met us in another year.
We name the times You brought us through—
There’s a story in each “thank You.”
May our children tell these stories, too,
And teach their own to turn to You.
Before we hang the lights this year.

[Outro: almost whispered, piano alone]
The boys bow their heads.
I hold Dawn’s hand.
For all You’ve brought us through…
Thank You.

[End]

albums/hold-the-line/.title: Steel and Nail Prints
albums/hold-the-line/.text:
[Intro]
[Lone bugle, soft military snare]

[Verse 1]
The flag snapped high over Pearl Harbor,
My boy pulled my hand down the pier.
He ran to the guns on the Missouri,
Said, "Dad, how'd they ever get these here?"
Nine barrels long as a schoolhouse,
Shells that weighed as much as a car.
He said, "Nothing could ever beat this ship,"
I said, "Son, let me tell you who we are."

[Verse 2]
I knelt beside him on the teakwood,
Pointed where the Arizona lay,
Told him men stood their post when the bombs fell
And gave everything they had that day.
Then I knocked on the side of that gray steel,
Said, "The guns aren't what made her great."

[Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Verse 3]
He said, "Dad, is that why you're so tough?"
I said, "Son, that strength's not my own.
God gave us these shoulders on purpose,
Rugged hands and a will like stone.
You may never go to war, son,
But there's another war around us all.
A man fights for his wife and his children,
And for the souls who are dying lost.
Some days you'll feel like quitting,
Like the waves are pulling you down,
But with His help you won't be sinking,
He's the One who holds you now."

[Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Bridge]
He had more power than any battleship,
Could've called twelve legions down,
But He held His fire on that hill
And took the hits without a sound.
They raised Him on a cross like a target,
And every sin of the world opened fire.
By His stripes, we are healed,
By His scars, we stand.
If you want to know what a real man looks like,
Look at the nail prints in His hands.

[Verse 4]
Thirty years and a few battle scars later,
I'm the one walking down that pier.
My own boy runs ahead to the cannons,
And I can almost feel Dad here.
I knock on the side of that gray steel,
Hear his words come out of me:
"Son, the guns aren't what made her great,
It's the hits she took to keep us free."

[Final Chorus]
She was built to take a hit and keep on sailing,
Built to hold her course through smoke and flame,
Not just made to dish it out, son,
But to take it all and fight again.
And God built a man the same way,
Gave him steel to stand his ground,
To stand between his family and the darkness,
Take the hit, and never go down.

[Outro]
[Bugle returns, soft]
Take the hit…
Like Jesus did.

[End]

singles/el-roi/.title: El Roi
singles/el-roi/.text:
[Spoken Intro: low female voice, solo piano]
You leave the hall light on all night,
And tell yourself he'll be alright.

[Pause]
The coffee's cold, you fold his shirt,
And swallow down another hurt.

Or at the sink, the water running,
You smile for them, and keep on going.
The kids ask, "Mom, is Daddy okay?"
You say, "He's fine," the same old way.

[Pause, spoken freely]
You remember the girl you were,
And the home you thought you'd build.

It never came.

You can't see past the strong one you pretend to be.

[Piano drops to one low note]
Look up.

[Verse 1: minor key, sparse piano and strings]
There was a woman sent away
With her boy and some water and bread.
And another woman, unloved,
Who named her sons for the love she dreamed instead.

[Low, almost spoken]
Nobody sees the unseen.

[Verse 2]
There was a woman mocked for years
For the child she couldn't bear.
And another went to the well at noon,
So no one else would see her there.

[Low, almost spoken]
Shame hides in plain sight.

[Verse 3]
There was a woman wed to a fool,
She paid for everything he'd done.
And another, widowed far from home,
Had nothing left, and no one.

[Low, almost spoken]
Carrying wears you down.

[Verse 4]
There was a woman who lost it all,
And told the town, "Call me Bitter now."
And another laughed at what God promised,
And took it in her hands somehow.

[Low, almost spoken]
Bitter says, "Too late."

[Chorus: stripped back, sorrowful]
We always thought He'd see some other girl,
Someone stronger, someone who could face the world.
We're the strong ones we pretend to be,
How could God see women like you and me?

[Spoken Bridge: piano only, almost a whisper]
"Thou tellest my wanderings:
Put thou my tears into thy bottle."

[Pause]

Then Someone saw their tears.

[Verse 5: key lifts, drums enter, strings begin to rise]
That woman sent away
Named the God who sees.
And that woman who named her sons for love
Bore the line that set us free.

Someone sees the unseen.

[Verse 6]
That woman mocked for years
Gave her son, and he led a nation.
And that woman at the well at noon
Ran back with an invitation.

Shame doesn't get the last word.

[Verse 7]
That woman wed to a fool
Rode out with food, and peace was made.
And that woman widowed far from home
Gleaned a field, and the line was laid.

Carrying isn't the end.

[Verse 8]
That woman who called herself Bitter
Held her grandson close, and smiled.
And that woman who laughed at the promise
Laughed again, like a child.

Hope says, "Not too late."

[Chorus: full band, strong vocal]
There was no other girl,
Just the unseen, the ashamed, the worn out.
They were never the strong ones,
But the One who sees made them seen.

[Spoken Reveal: slow, soft piano, one name per drum hit, pause between names]
Hagar.
Leah.
Hannah.
The woman at the well.
Abigail.
Ruth.
Naomi.
Sarah.

[Drums stop]
Women who wept.
Women who waited.
And God still saw their names.

[Pause, quiet]
"God hath chosen the weak things of the world
To confound the things which are mighty."

[Final Verse: quiet choir enters, gradually building]
And somewhere tonight a woman's awake,
The hall light on, the house gone still.
The smile she's practiced, the "I'm fine" she says,
The prayer she stopped against her will.

The tears in the shower so no one hears,
The weight she carries on her own.
The voice that says, "No one sees you, no one knows."

[Brief silence]
Look up. Someone sees you.

[Final Chorus: full band and choir, triumphant key lift]
There was no other girl,
It was never the strength of the woman.
We're not as strong as we pretend,
But He's the God who sees us now.

The true Strong One shining through
Every weary heart He holds.
We've got nothing left to hide.
Here we are, Lord. Hold us now.

[Spoken: band softens, sustained choir]
"The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart."

[Outro: piano alone, very quiet]
"Thou God seest me."

[Long pause]
Look up.

[End]

singles/enough/.title: Enough
singles/enough/.text:
[Verse 1 — Solo Baritone]
I’ve asked for more so many times,
With blessings all around.
I’ve watched what other people have
And missed what I have found.

Tonight I bring a different prayer;
Lord, teach my heart to see
The daily bread within my hands,
The grace You’ve given me.

[Chorus — Four-Part Male Harmony]
Give me enough to share my bread,
Enough to meet today.
Keep me from pride when I am fed,
From fear that leads astray.
And when Your answer fills my hands,
Keep gratitude within.
Lord, teach my heart to know enough
And thank You once again.

[Verse 2 — Baritone Lead, Gentle Bass Enters]
Give neither poverty nor wealth
That draws my heart from You.
When hunger puts my faith to test,
Lord, keep my footsteps true.

And when the cupboards all are full,
Keep me from asking more
While someone near me waits for help
Outside my quiet door.

[Chorus — Full Male Harmony]
Give me enough to share my bread,
Enough to meet today.
Keep me from pride when I am fed,
From fear that leads astray.
And when Your answer fills my hands,
Keep gratitude within.
Lord, teach my heart to know enough
And thank You once again.

[Verse 3 — Tenor Lead, Warm Harmonies]
There may be work for me to do,
There may be help to take.
Give me the grace to welcome both,
Whatever road You make.

And if You give me more to hold
Than what my household needs,
Lord, keep my hands from closing tight;
Let mercy shape my deeds.

[Bridge — Solo Baritone, Then Voices Enter]
When there is little, hear my prayer.
When there is much, stay near.
In every season, keep me Yours;
Your love has brought me here.

The bread will feed us for a day;
Tomorrow comes anew.
Whatever waits beyond this night,
We still depend on You.

[Final Chorus — Rich, Restrained Harmony]
Give me enough to share my bread,
Enough to meet today.
Keep me from pride when I am fed,
From fear that leads astray.
And when Your answer fills my hands,
Keep gratitude within.
Lord, teach my heart to know enough
And thank You once again.

[Outro — Soft Male Harmony]
For daily bread, for saving grace,
For those we love so much—
Receive our thanks, and teach our hearts
The quiet joy of enough.

[Soft, Sustained Amen]

singles/still-a-reason/.title: Still A Reason
singles/still-a-reason/.text:
[Verse 1 — Female Solo, Gentle Violin]
The groceries cost a little more;
The car needs gas again.
We bring our worries through the door,
Then whisper our amen.

With Christmas coming into view,
We fear what we can spend.
Lord, help us see Your gifts anew
Before this day shall end.

[Chorus — Women’s Harmonies]
There’s still a reason to give thanks,
A mercy we can name.
Through every burden that we bear,
Your love is still the same.
We bring the needs we cannot meet
And all we hope to do.
With grateful hearts we bow our heads
And put our trust in You.

[Verse 2 — Acoustic Guitar Enters]
Tomorrow calls us back to work
Before the morning light,
To serve the crowds and do our best
Till Friday turns to night.

When kindness meets a sharp reply
And patience wears away,
Lord, help us see each weary soul
And offer grace today.

[Chorus — Female Lead and Women’s Ensemble]
There’s still a reason to give thanks,
A mercy we can name.
Through every burden that we bear,
Your love is still the same.
We bring the needs we cannot meet
And all we hope to do.
With grateful hearts we bow our heads
And put our trust in You.

[Verse 3 — Warm, Intimate]
Across the table, children’s eyes
Look up to meet our own.
They hear us speak of rising costs
And worries yet unknown.

So let them hear us giving thanks
For blessings old and new,
And learn from how we live each day
To place their trust in You.

[Brief Violin Interlude]

[Verse 4 — Building]
When gifts we wish that we could buy
Are more than we can give,
Remind us of the gift of Christ,
Who died that we might live.

He knows the burdens that we bear,
The fears we’ve never shown.
And through the days we cannot see,
We will not walk alone.

[Final Chorus — Entirely A Cappella]
There’s still a reason to give thanks,
A mercy we can name.
Through every burden that we bear,
Your love is still the same.
We bring the needs we cannot meet
And all we hope to do.
With grateful hearts we bow our heads
And put our trust in You.

[Soft Harmonized Ending]
And put our trust in You.
Amen.

albums/battle-scars/.title: Everyone’s Story
albums/battle-scars/.text:
[Verse 1]
There's an old man in the last pew,
Hands that shake when he prays.
There's a widow at the counter
With her coffee gone cold.
There's a boy beside the window
Who won't say what's on his mind.
Every face I pass is a chapter
I've never been told.

[Verse 2]
There's a mama by a hospital bed
Holding on through the night.
There's a soldier home from a war
That never let him sleep.
There's a father who loves his son
But never found the words,
And a hundred thousand stories
That nobody hears.

[Chorus]
Everybody's got a story,
Every heart's a book half-read.
Some are written down in glory,
Some in scars and things unsaid.
But the Author's not finished,
Every page is in His hand.
Everybody's got a story,
And He's writing every one.

[Verse 3]
I kept mine locked up for years,
Thought it was too heavy to share,
Too much grief and too much failing
For anyone to care.
Then I let the words come out
And I heard them sung aloud,
And my wife cried, and my boys cried,
And I wasn't alone.

[Chorus]
Everybody's got a story,
Every heart's a book half-read.
Some are written down in glory,
Some in scars and things unsaid.
But the Author's not finished,
Every page is in His hand.
Everybody's got a story,
And He's writing every one.

[Bridge]
Paul said we're His workmanship,
The old word there is "poem."
Every life a verse He's writing,
Every scar a line.
So don't you close the cover
On the chapter that you hate,
Because the Author's not done writing,
And the ending's saved by grace.

[Final Chorus]
Everybody's got a story,
Tell yours, don't hold it in.
Somebody out there needs the chapter
That you've been afraid to share.
'Cause the Author's not finished,
Every page is in His hand.
Everybody's got a story,
And He's writing every one.

[Outro]
[Soft, spoken]
Let the redeemed of the Lord say so.

[End]

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Remember Thanksgiving
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1]
One year all we had was pizza,
And things were hard back then.
We bowed our heads around the table.
I can still hear us say amen.

[Verse 2]
On other Thanksgivings, when we were boys,
My brother and I built cabins on the floor.
Lincoln Logs scattered all around us,
While the smell of stuffing drifted through the door.

I’d head to the kitchen to help Mom.
She made it like Grandma showed her how.
After supper we’d play Monopoly.
I can almost hear us laughing now.

[Chorus]
Do you remember Thanksgiving?
Stay here a little while.
Put down the phone and tell me
What still makes you smile.
Before we make our Christmas lists,
Before this day is done,
Let’s count the things we’re thankful for
And take our time with every one.

[Verse 3]
The seeds we planted in springtime
Have ripened in the autumn sun.
We thank You, Lord, for what we gathered,
And for what You brought us from.

We remember the years we had plenty,
And the years we just got by.
Some of the gifts we thank You for now
Took us years to recognize.

[Bridge]
“God bless us, every one,”
I still hear Tiny Tim say.
But we’ve forgotten to thank You
For all the gifts You’ve given.
Before we ask for one thing more,
Lord, let us name them one by one.

[Final Chorus]
Do you remember Thanksgiving?
Stay here a little while.
What has the Lord brought you through
That you can thank Him for tonight?

[Short Piano Pause]

Before we make our Christmas lists,
Before this day is done,
Let’s count the things we’re thankful for
And take our time with every one.

[Outro]
One year all we had was pizza.
Thank You, Lord, for who was there.

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: The Worst Thanksgiving
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Grandma]
The plates are cleared, the coffee’s poured;
The grown-ups settle in.
The kids are playing Monopoly,
Each sure that they can win.

I asked what they were thankful for.
One called out from his chair,
“That after Dad deep-fried the bird,
Our house was still right there.”

[Grandma — Spoken, Quoting Dad]
“He took a sip and said, ‘It was just the porch.’”

[Chorus — Grandma and Grandpa]
Will we ever have
A perfect Thanksgiving?
Well, we can try again next year.
Maybe then we won’t burn the turkey
And keep the fire trucks out of here.
Pour another cup of coffee;
Nobody was laughing then.
Funny how the worst Thanksgiving
Is the one we tell again.

[Verse 2 — Grandma]
Their mama burned her first roast bird;
The skin was black as coal.
Her husband praised the mashed potatoes,
Then reached back for the bowl.

Another year she called me up:
“That bird’s still frozen through.”
I said, “Just grab your pie and come.
We’ve got enough for you.”

[Grandma — Spoken]
“She calls that her worst Thanksgiving. Me? I got two pies out of it.”

[Verse 3 — Grandma]
See that boy who bought up Boardwalk?
When he was only five,
The turkey up and disappeared.
You’d think it was alive.

His folks went looking through the house
And found him by the tub.
His rubber duck was floating there;
The bird was getting scrubbed.

[Grandma — Spoken, Quoting the Boy]
“He said, ‘I haven’t washed his back yet.’”

[Short Guitar Fill]

[Verse 4 — Grandma]
First year his folks had us for dinner,
The pies were put away.
His brother swore the dog ate all
The ones we’d baked that day.

He looked me squarely in the eye;
He almost got his way.
Then I saw pumpkin on his nose.
That gave the game away.

[Grandma — Spoken]
“I said, ‘The dog ate all of it?’ He said, ‘No. I left you the crusts.’”

[Final Chorus — Grandma and Grandpa]
Will we ever have
A perfect Thanksgiving?
Well, we can try again next year.
Maybe then we won’t burn the turkey
And keep the fire trucks out of here.
Pour another cup of coffee;
Nobody was laughing then.
Funny how the worst Thanksgiving
Is the one we tell again.

[Band Stops]

[Grandma — Spoken]
“Well, Pa, what about you? What’re ya thankful for?”

[Grandpa — Spoken, Deadpan]
“Turkey.”

[Beat]

“And supper’s been over an hour… and you’re all still here.”

[Pause]

“And I’m thankful for another year.”

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Altars Along The Way
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Intro — Slow, Haunting Piano and Solo Violin]

[Verse 1 — Young Son, Hushed and Worried]
Thanksgiving week, I woke to hear
A whisper down the hall.
I found my parents kneeling there;
Their shadows crossed the wall.

My sister followed close behind,
Her blanket trailing low.
Mom wiped a tear; Dad held her hand.
We whispered our hello.

[Daughter — Softly Spoken]
“Why is Mommy crying?”

[Mother — Sung, Tender and Slightly Trembling]
“We’ve had a lot upon our minds;
Some bills are coming due.
Come here, sweetheart, and sit with us.
There’s room for both of you.”

[Son — Softly Spoken]
“Are we going to be okay?”

[Verse 2 — Father, Warm and Steady]
“There’s nothing in the bank tonight;
We’ve paid what we could pay.
We’ve saved enough for pizza, though,
To share Thanksgiving Day.

When Mom and I were newly wed,
We faced some nights like these.
We brought our fears and every doubt
To God upon our knees.

And when you two were very small,
There were some lean years too.
You couldn’t understand it all,
But God brought us all through.

I’ve learned to watch when things get hard
For help I hadn’t planned.
So often, through another’s love,
I’ve recognized His hand.

We don’t know how the help will come,
Or when we’ll understand.
But God has heard our prayers before;
We’re safe within His hands.”

[Son — Softly Spoken]
“Daddy… can we pray too?”

[Father — Gently Sung]
“Come kneel down here with Mom and me;
There’s room on either side.
You needn’t carry all this care;
We trust Him to provide.”

[Chorus — Adult Male Lead, Gentle Female Harmonies]
Altars along the way,
The stories we will share,
So those who follow us will know
That God has met us there.
We’ll bring our children close to pray,
Through questions, fears, and tears,
And help them see His fingerprints
Across the passing years.

[Verse 3 — Son, Quiet and Hopeful]
I asked the Lord to help my dad
And help my mom sleep too.
My sister folded both her hands
And whispered, “We need You.”

We rose and turned the lamplight out;
Our worries weren’t all gone.
But I had seen my father’s faith
And something to lean on.

[Violin Interlude — Hope Begins to Rise]

[Verse 4 — Son, Thanksgiving Morning]
I woke to something warm and sweet
And hurried down the stair.
My sister followed close behind,
Still holding to her bear.

The turkey browned, the bread was warm;
I couldn’t help but stare.
We’d gone to bed with little left;
Now there was food to share.

[Music Brightens — Acoustic Guitar and Gentle Rhythm Enter]

[Verse 5 — Son]
We helped to bring the dishes in;
Mom took her favorite chair.
Dad caught our eyes across the meal,
Then paused before the prayer.

[Father — Sung With Quiet Joy]
“Last night a friend brought groceries
And knocked upon our door.
They’d bought a turkey big enough
For two households or more.

They didn’t know our bank was bare,
Or what we’d knelt to say.
But there they stood with food to share
For our Thanksgiving Day.”

[Father — Warm, With a Knowing Smile]
“Remember kneeling by the couch,
The things we couldn’t see?
Now look around this table, kids,
And tell me what you see.”

[Daughter — Softly Spoken, Wondering]
“He heard us, Daddy.”

[Son — Softly Spoken]
“Just like when we were little?”

[Father — Warmly Spoken]
“Just like then.
And this time, you’ll remember.”

[Chorus — Fuller and Warmer, Tempo Lifting]
Altars along the way,
The stories we will share,
So those who follow us will know
That God has met us there.
We’ll bring our children close to pray,
Through questions, fears, and tears,
And help them see His fingerprints
Across the passing years.

[Bridge — Adult Son, Years Later]
Now I’m the father kneeling down;
My children hear me pray.
I think about that little room
And what Dad used to say.

I tell them what we’re facing now,
Then make room at my side.
We bring our needs to God as one
And trust Him to provide.

And when His answer comes, we stop
Before we rush away.
We name the mercy we’ve received
And thank Him when we pray.

[Final Chorus — Faster, Joyful Family Harmonies]
Altars along the way,
The stories we will share,
So those who follow us will know
That God has met us there.
Come gather close and hear us tell
Of grace through all these years.
We’ve learned to see His fingerprints
Through laughter and through tears.

[Outro — Child’s Voice, Bright and Hopeful]
“Dad… remember when we prayed?”

[Father — Warmly Spoken]
“I do, son.
Let’s thank Him again.”

[Family Harmonies]
For all the ways You’ve brought us through,
For mercies old and new,
We’ll tell the ones who follow us
How we have trusted You.

[Joyful Violin Ending]

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Save Us A Chair!
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Adult Male Lead]
We played a little football first
Till someone hollered, “Chow!”
The guy who dropped the winning catch
Still blames the sunshine now.

The cook came out with turkey, boys;
We all let out a cheer.
He said, “Your mama’s got me beat,
But mine’ll do this year.”

[Chorus — Lead and Group Voices]
Thanksgiving in uniform,
Half a world away.
We’re passing plates and telling tales
Of home on Thanksgiving Day.
Here’s to home and here’s to freedom,
And the folks who miss us there.
Till we’re back beneath our own porch lights,
Back home, save us a chair.

[Verse 2 — Adult Male Lead]
One told us how his granddad used
To carve the bird each year.
Another said, “To get some pie,
You’d best shift into gear.”

I told ’em how my youngest keeps
One eye cracked during grace.
Her brother stole her roll last year;
She’s guarding hers in place.

[Chorus — Lead and Group Voices]
Thanksgiving in uniform,
Half a world away.
We’re passing plates and telling tales
Of home on Thanksgiving Day.
Here’s to home and here’s to freedom,
And the folks who miss us there.
Till we’re back beneath our own porch lights,
Back home, save us a chair.

[Bridge — Dad Sings, Band Pulls Back]
I called while they were setting plates;
My girl picked up the phone.
She asked me what I’d like to eat
The day that I got home.

I said, “It doesn’t matter, kid,
What’s waiting at the door.
Just save a place right next to you;
I couldn’t ask for more.”

[Final Verse — Young Daughter Sings Solo, Soft Guitar]
Dad, I saved your seat beside me
This Thanksgiving Day.
I wish that you were here with us;
You’re half a world away.

We bowed our heads to say our thanks,
The way you taught us to.
I thanked the Lord that we are free,
Then said a prayer for you.

[Final Chorus — Adult Male Lead and Full Group Vocals]
Thanksgiving in uniform,
Half a world away.
We’re passing plates and telling tales
Of home on Thanksgiving Day.
Here’s to home and here’s to freedom,
To the flag we’re proud to wear.
Till we’re back beneath our own porch lights,
Back home, save us a chair!

[Outro — Group Voices]
Back home, save us a chair.

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Are You Still Thankful
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Soft, Searching]
There was a shoreline.
There was a grave.
There were the people
God helped sustain.

Then came the harvest,
Corn, fowl, and deer.
Neighbors sat with them.
Thanks mingled with tears.

[Pre-Chorus]
They knew the hunger.
They knew the cost.
Even in plenty,
They knew what they’d lost.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 2 — Slowly Building]
There was a nation,
Newly made free.
Washington called us
To bow gratefully.

Then came division,
Brothers at war.
Lincoln called wounded
Hearts to the Lord.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for His mercy,
Prayer for our land.
Even in sorrow,
We needed His hand.

[Chorus]
Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.
There are no presents,
Just thankfulness.

Bread on the table,
One day to live.
Still we depend on
The God who gives.

[Verse 3 — Warm, Bittersweet]
Nineteen-fifty.
Chairs on the floor.
Grandma is coming;
One place for more.

Bread from the oven,
Hands worn with care.
Dad bows his head now.
We hear his prayer.

[Pre-Chorus]
Thanks for the wages,
Thanks for the rain,
Thanks for the mercy
That brought us again.

[Verse 4 — Growing Urgency]
Now there is plenty,
More than we need.
Phones at the table,
No time to speak.

Christmas is calling.
Sales fill the screen.
We’re making our wishes.
What does thanks mean?

[Bridge — Exposed Voice]
Why did we gather?
What was this for?
When did our blessings
Leave us wanting more?

Lord, I’ve been asking.
Lord, I’ve forgot
How much You’ve given,
How much it cost.

[Final Chorus — Full, Aching]
Are we still thankful?
Lord, help us say yes.
More than a dinner,
More than a guest.

You give the harvest.
You give us breath.
Still we depend on
Your faithfulness.

[Outro — Quiet]
Before it is Christmas,
Let us stay here.
Thank You for mercy
Through all these years.

Are you still thankful?
Please tell me yes.

[Let the final piano chord fade]

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: A Thanksgiving Carol
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Wednesday Night]
The kids were down by half past eight.
The turkey had finally thawed.
They’d scraped up enough for Thanksgiving Day.
For Christmas, there was nothing to put away.

He spread the bills across his knees.
She went upstairs to cry.
The boys had circled what they wanted most.
She turned their lists face down and reached for a quilt.

A box came down and hit the floor.
Two albums slid out side by side.
There was her brother, grinning ear to ear,
Giving her rabbit ears through all those years.

And she laughed.

[Verse 2 — Thanksgiving Past]
She brought the box down to the couch.
“Look at Mom there by the stove.
I never saw how tired she looked.
I just remember how she sang while she cooked.”

He opened up the other book.
Dad wore his work shirt in the frame.
“He always said he’d missed the day.
I remember he sat down to play.”

[Chorus]
Look what we have right here.
It took a picture to make it clear.
Lord, give us eyes to see today
Before it slips into yesterday.
We don’t know what tomorrow holds.
There’s plenty we can’t see.
But thank You for this day
And for who’s here with me.

[Verse 3 — Thanksgiving Yet to Come]
For a minute she could see their boy
With a little boy of his own.
He held a picture they hadn’t taken yet:
“One Thanksgiving I won’t forget.”

“See Grandma there beside me?
She took most of the pictures back then.
That time she started to step away,
Then I heard her say, ‘Wait for me.’”

[Bridge — Back to Wednesday Night]
The furnace clicked. She looked around.
The bills were still across his knees.
He said, “I don’t know how we’ll make it through.”
She said, “I don’t know about Christmas, too.”

Then she said, “We’ve got enough for tomorrow.”
He sat a while and held her hand.
“Lord, thank You for what’s in this house.”
And that was all the prayer they had.

[Thanksgiving Day — music pulls back]
After pie, one of the boys
Held up his phone. “Everybody squeeze.”
She stepped aside the way she always did.
Then turned around. “Hey, wait for me.”

[Final Verse — Black Friday]
Friday morning, at the table,
His phone lit up beside the bills.
“One day only,” flashed across the screen.
He swiped it off to find a different scene.

There they were, all squeezed together.
She set his coffee down.
“Still don’t know how we’ll make December work.”
He said, “I know,” and slid the phone to her.

[Final Chorus]
Look what we have right here.
It took a picture to make it clear.
Lord, give us eyes to see today
Before it slips into yesterday.
We don’t know what December holds.
There’s plenty we can’t see.
But thank You for this day
And for who’s here with me.

[Spoken, after the music falls away]
That was a good day.

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Dancing In The Porch Light
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Husband]
Thanksgiving’s done, the house is still;
The kids are tucked away.
You’re at the sink, still washing pans;
You’ve been on your feet all day.

The first few flakes catch in the light;
I reach to take your hand.
“Come see the snow. The pans can wait.”
You say, “You gonna dance?”

[Chorus — Together]
Dancing in the porchlight,
Snow falling soft and slow.
This year asked more of both of us
Than most folks ever know.
We didn’t get it all quite right,
But we made it through.
And if I don’t say it near enough,
I couldn’t do it without you.

[Verse 2 — Wife]
You still remember losing hold
Of what you meant to say.
I saw you knock on their bedroom door
And make it right that day.

And when your hours got cut last spring,
I knew you lay awake.
Tonight the boys pulled up a chair
And begged you for one more game.

[Verse 3 — Husband]
You said the rolls were burned again;
I ate two anyway.
Then your sister called and said
She’d spend the night alone that day.

You drove across the county line
And brought her home to eat.
By pie she had us laughing
So hard we couldn’t speak.

[Bridge — Trading Lines, Softly]
[Wife]
Thank You for the kids asleep
And the laughter down the hall.

[Husband]
Thank You for the freedom, Lord,
To bow our heads at all.

[Wife]
Thank You for the faith to pray
When we could see no way.

[Husband]
Thank You for the hand in mine
At the end of Thanksgiving Day.

[Final Chorus — Together]
Dancing in the porchlight,
Snow falling soft and slow.
This year asked more of both of us
Than most folks ever know.
We didn’t get it all quite right,
But we made it through.
And if I don’t say it near enough,
I couldn’t do it without you.

[Outro — Wife, Softly Spoken]
“Don’t let go yet.”

albums/remember-thanksgiving/.title: Present On The Tree
albums/remember-thanksgiving/.text:
[Verse 1 — Warm Male Lead]
Thanksgiving supper’s over now;
The boys get up to clear.
I say, “The dishes all can wait.
Just stay a minute here.”

My parents told me long ago
How Christmas used to be:
No fancy gifts from any store,
Just little presents on the tree.

[Chorus]
Lord, let the thanks we gave today
Go with us when we sing
Of Christ who in a manger lay,
Our Savior and our King.

The hands we folded for our bread
We fold again in prayer.
We thank You for Your only Son
And all He came to bear.

[Verse 2 — Like Telling a Story]
There’s an old story I once heard
Of two with little there:
She bought a chain to fit his watch
With money from her hair.

He sold his watch to buy the combs
She’d hoped for Christmas Day.
The combs and chain could wait awhile;
Look what they gave away.

[Verse 3 — A Little Warmer]
There’s an old Christmas film I love
About a man brought low.
He thinks no one would miss him much,
Then friends begin to show.

They crowd the room on Christmas Eve
And give what they can spare.
He sees how wonderful life is
With all his loved ones there.

[Turn — Music Pulls Back]
I look across the table now
At faces dear to me.
“Boys, let the thanks we gave for bread
Go with us to the tree.”

[Bridge — Guitar and One Voice]
The hands that Mary held that night,
So small against her own,
Would one day bear the nails for us.
No greater love was shown.

The greatest gift hung on a tree:
Christ died to take our place.
No price we pay, no work we do
Could earn that gift of grace.

A gift can have your name on it
And still be left behind.
By faith receive the gift of Christ;
In Him new life you’ll find.

[Final Chorus — Warm Family Harmonies]
Lord, let the thanks we gave today
Go with us when we sing
Of Christ who in a manger lay,
Our Savior and our King.

The hands we folded for our bread
We fold again in prayer.
We thank You for Your only Son
And all He came to bear.

[Outro — Dad Alone]
“Now, boys, we’ll get the lights down soon.
Just sit a while with me.”
We thank You, Father, for the child
Who gave Himself upon the tree.
